chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Do not eat the eel, nor the sea horse, nor the floating one, nor the spleen, because it is the house of blood and a morsel of Satan.
Because it is the house of blood and a morsel of Satan.

key_terms.طَافِيًا: The floating one (a type of fish)

ai.seo_question: What specific foods are prohibited in Shia Islam according to the hadith of Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prohibits the consumption of eels, sea horses, floating fish, and spleen, describing them as 'houses of blood' and 'morsels of Satan.' This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of *khalal* (impurity) derived from high blood content and spiritual impurity, distinguishing these items from permissible seafood. The description 'morsels of Satan' highlights the metaphysical dimension of dietary laws in Shia tradition, linking physical consumption to spiritual well-being.
